messages:
alicia: fyi running a long-context stress on mi250x and I'm seeing VRAM climb steadily even with expected evicts. kvcache free list size increases, but pagetable shows lots of 'tombstone' entries. repro attached below.
max: can you paste the repro command? also which model/config?
alicia: short command: ```./run_repro.sh --model llama-7b --ctx 131072 --batch 4 --gpu mi250x --paged-attn true --seed 42```
mira: hmm we've seen tombstone churn on MI when eviction ordering is slightly off vs NV. does the trace show evict callbacks completing?
alicia: partial trace snippet: 
```
[2026-02-10 14:02:11] kvcache: alloc page 0x7f12 size 256k owner=worker-3
[2026-02-10 14:02:11] pager: evict start page=10240 -> target_frame=8
[2026-02-10 14:02:11] pager: mark tombstone page=10240 owner=null
[2026-02-10 14:02:12] kvcache: free-list.len=128
[2026-02-10 14:02:12] kvcache: alloc page 0x7f14 (reused?) page=10240 owner=worker-1
[2026-02-10 14:02:12] pagetable: hole_count=27 tombstone_count=83
```
ryan: interesting - looks like reuse is picking up tombstoned pages before underlying PTEs are fully recycled. could be a memory fence/order issue on MI PCI path.
max: do you see any failed kernel launches or retries in the job log?
alicia: no kernel failures. Kernel selection prints: `kernels: attention_paged_v2(mi_opt) fallback=attention_paged_v1` and it's selecting mi_opt consistently. Perf numbers (first 30m): tokens/s drops ~8% over time.
mira: that perf regression matches the VRAM pressure hypothesis -- more fragmentation -> smaller contiguous allocs -> suboptimal kernel paths (fallback path uses smaller tiled kernel)
ryan: quick experiment idea: change evict heuristic to prefer oldest contiguous-run pages instead of LRU-by-last-touch, to avoid scattering tombstones. low effort toggle in pager: `EVICT_POLICY=runpref`
max: can you try with `EVICT_POLICY=runpref` and `KV_CACHE_PREFETCH=0`? also run with `--ctx 65536` to see if growth only at extreme ctx sizes.
alicia: ran that for 10 minutes: with runpref VRAM stable-ish, free-list.len stays ~40 and tombstone_count drops to single digits. tokens/s stable. So heuristic change mitigates.
ryan: nice. That indicates the root isn't a HW driver bug but allocation fragmentation + reuse ordering. still want to be careful about races where two workers try to reclaim same page slot.
mira: can you get a repro trace with `KV_DEBUG=page-ops` (it prints atomic ops order)? paste if small.
alicia: pasted partial below: 
```
[atomics] CAS(page_slot=8, expected=0, desired=RECLAIMING) -> true
[atomics] XCHG(page_slot=8, old=RECLAIMING) -> TOMBSTONE
[atomics] CAS(page_slot=8, expected=TOMBSTONE, desired=ALLOC) -> true
[atomics] worker-1 assigned page_slot=8
```
alicia: seems CAS->XCHG sequence yields TOMBSTONE then immediate ALLOC by another worker, but pagetable metadata still references old page id until background compaction runs. we get a window where page is reused while metadata lags.
max: possible fixes: 1) stronger ordering when moving from TOMBSTONE->ALLOC (full fence + validate pagetable id) 2) delay reuse until compaction confirms pte cleared 3) change tombstone state machine to include a 'quarantine' slot.
ryan: 1) has perf cost on hot path, 2) might fix but adds tail latency, 3) quarantine seems promising: short TTL for tombstone to avoid immediate reuse but cheap.
mira: also we should add a metric for 'tombstone_reuse_count' and alert when > 10/min, to catch regressions.
alicia: created a small branch with runpref + quarantine TTL=50ms and added tombstone_reuse_count metric. benchmarks look good locally. pushing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3472 (draft) (react :eyes:)
pager-bot: CI run queued for PR 3472.
max: nice. for tracking can we open an internal ticket linking the MI250X trace and plan? i'll create ticket ENGRT-9487 and paste here.
alicia: ENGRT-9487 created: includes logs, tracers, and the quick mitigation. assigning to runtime oncall.
ryan: thanks, folks. next steps: prod canary with runpref + quarantine on a small shard, monitor tombstone_reuse_count and tokens/s for 6h. if stable, roll to all.
mira: would be good to test on H100 too just in case kernel fallback behavior differs.
alicia: will run on h100 tomorrow and update thread.
